_meta.purpose: 20 hand-built specs that are either physically impossible or need a costed fix. Ground truth is definitional here - unlike a defect-detection benchmark, nobody can argue with 'two devices cannot share I2C address 0x3C'. This is your eval set and your headline number.
_meta.how_to_report: verdict must be one of: REFUSE (fatal, no auto-fix), FIXED (auto-fix applied, report the change), WARN (built with a caveat), BUILD (valid). The solver's output must match expected_verdict and cite expected_rule.
_meta.headline: On 20 conflicting specs: X refused/fixed correctly, Y wrong, Z false refusals on the 3 positive controls.

cases.prompt: Build an ESP32 plant monitor with an SSD1306 OLED (0x3C) and a second SSD1306 OLED (0x3C) so I can see two screens.
cases.note: Classic. Fix: 0x3D variant, TCA9548A mux, or drop one.

cases.prompt: Add an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to my ESP32 and read the distance.
cases.note: ECHO idles at 5 V into a 3.3 V pin. Needs a level shifter.

cases.prompt: Control a servo from the ESP32 to open a valve.
cases.note: Servo power from the 3V3 rail will brown out the board.

cases.prompt: Read the soil moisture sensor on GPIO 13 and also send data over WiFi.
cases.note: GPIO 13 is ADC2 - invalid while WiFi is on. Move to ADC1 (32-39).

cases.prompt: Connect a servo signal to GPIO 34 on my ESP32.
cases.note: GPIO 34 is input-only.

cases.prompt: Use GPIO 11 for a button input.
cases.note: GPIO 11 is wired to the SPI flash.

cases.prompt: Put a temperature sensor on GPIO 4 and an OLED on the same pin too.
cases.note: One pin, two peripherals.

cases.prompt: Add an INA219 current sensor module.
cases.note: Not in the DB. Must refuse rather than guess - this is the integrity test.

cases.prompt: Drive a 4-channel relay module from the ESP32 to switch a pump.
cases.note: Inductive load. Flyback diode required.

cases.prompt: Power a WS2812B strip of 30 LEDs from the ESP32 board.
cases.note: 30 x 60 mA = 1.8 A. Never from 3V3.

cases.prompt: Power a WS2812B strip of 30 LEDs from the ESP32 board.
cases.note: Duplicate of C10 with different phrasing - tests robustness to paraphrase, and that you did not hardcode the prompt.

cases.prompt: Mount everything on a grid plate 100mm x 60mm: ESP32, OLED, DHT22, soil sensor, buzzer.
cases.note: Footprints do not fit 100x60 with clearance. Either enlarge the plate, stack, or use adapters.

cases.prompt: Show temperature on an OLED and read an MPU6050 IMU at the same time.
cases.note: POSITIVE CONTROL. 0x3C and 0x68 do not collide. Must NOT refuse, and no rule may fire.

cases.prompt: Read a DHT22 and show it on the OLED, plus a buzzer alert.
cases.note: Valid build, but the DHT22 data line needs a pull-up: the solver must offer one.

cases.prompt: Drive 6 servos plus 4 sensors from one ESP32 DevKitC.
cases.note: 6 x 250 mA stall = 1.5 A on one board. Offer PCA9685 + external supply.

cases.prompt: Use the ESP32 internal pull-up for the I2C bus.
cases.note: Internal pull-ups (~45 kOhm) are far too weak for I2C. Needs external 4.7k.

cases.prompt: Power a BME280 from the 5V breadboard rail.
cases.note: BME280 max supply is 3.6 V. Different direction of level mismatch.

cases.prompt: Drive a piezo buzzer from GPIO 2.
cases.note: GPIO 2 is a boot-strapping pin: the solver must move it.

cases.prompt: Make a device that shows the time on an OLED.
cases.note: POSITIVE CONTROL. Trivially valid - must not refuse. Guards against an over-eager validator.

cases.prompt: Print a custom enclosure that holds the ESP32, the OLED, the DHT22 and the soil sensor, 120mm x 80mm x 40mm.
cases.note: Valid layout but dimensions come from clone-typical data, so flag measurement uncertainty.
